findings.source_passage: She shrugged. 'Neither do I, but there's got to be a way. Maybe you could slap your mark or kiss it or do something.' My face fell. 'Seriously?'
findings.source_locator: After Heather suggests the mark, before she crosses her arms
findings.why_it_matters: Miriam's deadpan 'Seriously?' reaction beat and Heather's full shrug-and-hedge exchange establish the comic register of the friendship. The draft collapses this into a bare imperative list, losing the narrator's incredulous voice.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore Miriam's 'Seriously?' and the preceding shrug-and-hedge from Heather to preserve the comic timing.

findings.source_passage: 'She released my hands and stepped to the side where she crossed her arms. "It's all up to you now, Miriam. I got you here, now you've got to get that mark going." "All you did was drive me here!" I argued. "Close enough, now focus on that mark!"'
findings.source_locator: After 'My face fell. Seriously?' exchange, before Miriam looks at her shoulder
findings.why_it_matters: This micro-argument is a voice-defining beat: Miriam's pushback ('All you did was drive me here!') and Heather's dismissive 'Close enough' is the signature comic rhythm of their dynamic. The draft omits it entirely.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the 'All you did was drive me here!' / 'Close enough, now focus on that mark!' exchange before Miriam turns to her shoulder.

findings.source_passage: 'With a hope and a prayer I leapt into the void. The trip was exactly like the first one, but the exit was a little different. I stumbled out of the other side of the portal and onto the hard stone platform. The front of my foot betrayed me this time and I tripped on one of those rocks.'
findings.source_locator: Immediately after Heather steps aside, before the sage's shocked face
findings.why_it_matters: 'With a hope and a prayer' and 'The front of my foot betrayed me this time' are both register-defining — the first is a set-phrase beat that marks the narrator's voice; the second is the self-deprecating specificity that characterises Miriam throughout. The draft replaces them with a bare 'I leapt.'
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'With a hope and a prayer' as the launching phrase and add the 'front of my foot betrayed me' detail on landing.

findings.source_passage: 'Um, hi. You don't happen to-' My eyes noticed a large stain over the stones. The stain was a distinct red color. My heart quickened. I looked up at them. 'Where's Xander?'
findings.source_locator: After Miriam grins up at the sages, before Apuleius offers his hand
findings.why_it_matters: The interrupted comic opener ('Um, hi. You don't happen to-') cut by the sight of blood is an interpretively important beat: Miriam's breezy confidence collides with the gravity of Xander's situation. The draft jumps straight to the stain and the question, erasing the tonal collision.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the 'Um, hi. You don't happen to—' line so the interruption by the blood stain reads as the intended dramatic pivot.

findings.source_passage: 'I was up to bartering my soul for a reprieve from the wind whipping through my hair when we reached the castle.'
findings.source_locator: After Apuleius sweeps Miriam into his arms and they are airborne, before the guards with spears
findings.why_it_matters: 'Bartering my soul for a reprieve' is the narrator's hyperbolic interior voice — a small but characteristic comic aside during the flight. Its omission flattens the airborne passage.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the 'bartering my soul for a reprieve from the wind' line in the brief flight summary to keep Miriam's voice present.

summary: Four medium-severity voice/interpretive losses — including the deleted 'All you did was drive me here!' argument, the 'With a hope and a prayer' launch, the interrupted comic greeting before the blood stain, and the Heather 'Seriously?' beat — collectively erase enough of Miriam's signature ironic register to require regeneration.
